pattern_id: Mempool Flush uses read-lock while performing write operations causing data race
description: BUG PATTERN: Mempool Flush() uses read-lock (RLock) while performing write/mutating operations. DESCRIPTION: Code audit discovered that CListMempool.Flush() acquires a read-lock (RLock) but then performs write operations including removeTx() which mutates the data structure. Multiple goroutines can hold a read-lock simultaneously, so concurrent Flush() calls can corrupt data. This bug also indicates insufficient testing - a proper test suite with race detector would have caught this. ROOT CAUSE: Developer confusion between read and write operations, or copy-paste error. RLock allows concurrent access assuming no mutations, but Flush() clearly mutates state. The naming 'Flush' suggests clearing/writing, yet it uses a read-lock. LESSON: Lock usage patterns to verify: 1) RLock should ONLY be used for pure read operations with no side effects; 2) Any method that calls mutating helpers must use write lock; 3) Method names like Flush, Clear, Remove, Update are red flags for read-lock usage; 4) Code audits should specifically check lock type vs operation type; 5) Run race detector on ALL code paths, not just common ones - Flush may be rarely called making races hard to reproduce.
